questions.question: 1. Which property of a spring is determined from the slope of the Load–Deflection graph?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Young's modulus is a material property obtained from stress–strain tests.
explanations.b: Correct. The slope of the Load–Deflection graph represents the spring stiffness (spring constant).
explanations.c: Incorrect. Poisson's ratio is not obtained from the Load–Deflection graph.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Yield strength cannot be determined from this experiment.

questions.question: 2. When the applied load on a spring is doubled within the elastic limit, the deflection will:

explanations.a: Correct. According to Hooke's law, deflection is directly proportional to the applied load within the elastic range.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Deflection changes with the applied load.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The relationship is linear within the elastic limit.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Increasing the load does not reduce the deflection.

questions.question: 3. The energy stored in a compressed spring is called:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Kinetic energy is associated with motion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Gravitational potential energy is unrelated to spring deformation.
explanations.c: Correct. A spring stores elastic strain energy when compressed.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Thermal energy is not the quantity measured in this experiment.

questions.question: 4. If two springs are made from the same material and have the same dimensions except that one has a larger wire diameter, that spring will generally be:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Increasing the wire diameter increases spring stiffness.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A larger wire diameter makes the spring stiffer, not more flexible.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The spring continues to store strain energy.
explanations.d: Correct. A thicker spring wire increases the stiffness of the spring.

questions.question: 5. Which instrument is commonly used to measure the diameter of the spring wire?

explanations.a: Correct. A micrometer provides accurate measurement of the spring wire diameter.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A spring balance measures force.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A steel rule is not sufficiently precise for measuring wire diameter.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A dial gauge is used to measure displacement.

questions.question: 6. Which material property is used in the theoretical deflection equation of a close-coiled helical spring?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Young's modulus is not directly used in the spring deflection equation.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Bulk modulus relates to volumetric compression.
explanations.c: Correct. The deflection equation uses the modulus of rigidity because the spring wire is subjected mainly to torsion.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Density does not determine spring deflection.

questions.question: 7. A spring is subjected to a load of 240 N and undergoes a deflection of 24 mm. What is the spring stiffness?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This value does not satisfy the relation between load and deflection.
explanations.b: Correct. Spring stiffness = Load ÷ Deflection = 240 ÷ 24 = 10 N/mm.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This value is greater than the calculated stiffness.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This value is obtained by an incorrect calculation.

questions.question: 8. If the spring stiffness increases while the applied load remains constant, the spring deflection will:

explanations.a: Incorrect. A stiffer spring undergoes less deflection under the same load.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Deflection depends on both load and stiffness.
explanations.c: Correct. Since deflection equals load divided by stiffness, increasing stiffness reduces deflection.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The spring will still deform under load.

questions.question: 9. Why is the Load–Deflection relationship verified only within the elastic limit of the spring?

answers.a: Because permanent deformation may occur beyond the elastic limit.
answers.d: Because the modulus of rigidity becomes infinite.

explanations.a: Correct. Beyond the elastic limit, the spring may undergo permanent deformation and no longer obey Hooke's law.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The weight of the spring is unaffected by loading.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Torsional stress does not become zero under loading.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The modulus of rigidity is a material property and does not become infinite.
